chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-A'ala ibn Al-Muqadd, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'An angel is assigned to the Yamani corner since Allah created the heavens and the earth; he has no constant task (hijjir) except saying Ameen to your supplications. So let a servant consider what he is supplicating for.' I said to him, 'What is the hijjir?' He said, 'It is a word from the speech of the Arabs, meaning there is no work for him [other than that].' And in another report, 'There is no work for him apart from that.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِيُّ: The Yamani Corner of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What is the role of the angel at the Yamani corner of the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Yamani corner (Rukn al-Yamani) as a unique locus of divine acceptance, where an angel has been stationed since creation solely to affirm the supplications of pilgrims. The term 'hijjir' is clarified as meaning 'work' or 'action,' emphasizing that the angel's exclusive function is to say 'Ameen,' thereby encouraging worshippers to be deliberate and mindful in their du'as. This underscores the Shia scholarly view of the Kaaba's corners not merely as physical landmarks but as spiritual conduits for divine response.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al A’ala Bin Al Muqa’ad who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘An Angel has been Allocated with the Yamani corner since Allahazwj Created the skies and the firmaments, there not being anything constantly for him to do except for saying ‘Ameen’ upon your supplication. So let a servant look into what he is supplicating for’. So, I said to himasws, ‘What is Al-Hijjir?’ So heasws said: ‘It is an expression from the expression of the Arabs meaning that there is no (other) work for him to do’. And in another report, ‘(Heasws said): ‘There is no work for him apart from that’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from al-‘ Ala’ ibn al-Muq‘ad who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘There is an angel assigned on al-Yemaniy corner from the time Allah created the heavens and the earth. This angel has no Hijjir except saying, ‘Amen’ for your prayers, so a servant of Allah should consider what to appeal for in his prayer.’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘What is al-Hijjir?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is the expression of Arabs, meaning he has nothing to do but to do so and so. In another Hadith it says, ‘He (the angel) has no other task but that (saying Amen)”’
